To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Shb links SLP76, Gads (and Vav) with the CD3-complex in Jurkat T-cells and that Shb is targeted, via its SH2 domain, to GEMs after TCR stimulation.
Shb links the T cell receptor with the SLP-75-Vav complex in Jurkat cells and that this interaction is mediated by the SH2 and SH3 domains of Shb.
Shb is involved in the TCR signaling complex by recruiting SLP-76/GADS/VAV to the TCR zeta-chain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Shb in the T cell signalling pathway.
the molecular mechanism(s) by which Shb regulates T cell activation and function.
the interactions of the adaptor protein Shp with the SLP-75-Vav-Gads complex and how Shb aids in the activation of this complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Shb is a critical adaptor molecule that is involved in the initial events in T cell activation.
Shb acts as a scaffold to link the TCR complex to the SLP- 76-Gads-VAV complex, thereby facilitating the assembly of a functional signalling complex.
Shb is a critical adaptor protein that links the T cell receptor with the SLP-75-Gads-Vav signaling module.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Shb is a key player in the early events of T cell activation and is involved in the assembly of the TCR complex.
Shb is a scaffold protein, which links ZAP70, SLP-76/Gads and Vav to the TCR complex.
Shb is a novel adapter protein in T cells, which plays a role in the recruitment of SLP- 76, Vav and Gads to the TCR zeta-chain and the ZAP70 tyrosine kinase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Shb acts as a scaffold protein that brings together the SLP- 76, Gads-Vav complex and the TCR complex.
Shb plays an important role in linking the SLP- 76-Gads-VAV complex with the TCR complex.
Shb plays a critical role as a linker molecule between ZAP70, SLP-76/Gads and Vav in TCR signalling.
